title: n4fl9o
Caliph Abu Bakr's Appointment of Caliph Umar and the Six-Man Shura
hook: Caliph Abu Bakr left Caliph Umar in his place. Caliph Umar in turn gave the matter to six people; this shura is narrated in Bukhari.
scenes.0.text: When Caliph Abu Bakr sensed that death was drawing near in Medina, he left Caliph Umar in his place. The rule hastily established at Saqifa passed from Abu Bakr to Umar. **Imam Ali** was not called to this appointment. His right proclaimed at Ghadir was again ignored.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.1.text: Before the appointment, Abu Bakr consulted Abd al-Rahman and Uthman. A group spoke of Caliph Umar's harshness. "What will you answer your Lord?" was said. Talha also objected. Abu Bakr declared that he would tell God he had chosen the best of His servants. Imam Ali was not among those consulted. His name was not asked.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: s20l3t
Talha
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: p9t1xw
Abu Bakr
scenes.2.text: Abu Bakr died. From the Prophet's death until 22 Jumada al-Akhira 13, he had remained caliph for about two years and three months. Umar became caliph in Medina. The conquests expanded. **Imam Ali** lived in Medina and was one of those consulted. His being consulted was not a substitute for his right at Ghadir. Imam Ali was patient and stayed in his house.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.3.text: In Medina, Caliph Umar was stabbed with a dagger at the morning prayer. He died on 26 Dhu al-Hijja 23. His caliphate had lasted about ten years and six months. The attacker wounded thirteen people. Umar did not choose his successor alone. He would leave the matter to six people. **Imam Ali** would be counted among those six, yet would still be left outside the caliphate.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.4.text: The wounded Caliph Umar named six people: **Imam Ali**, Uthman, Zubayr, Talha, Sa'd and Abd al-Rahman. His son Abdullah would be a witness. He would have no share in the caliphate. **Imam Ali**, whose right was proclaimed at Ghadir, was made a member of this council.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1m9a3ex
Uthman
scenes.4.art.actors.2.label: 18i2n4z
Abd al-Rahman b. Awf
scenes.5.text: In the six-man council, Zubayr and Talha yielded their rights in favor of **Imam Ali** and Uthman. Sa'd withdrew in favor of Abd al-Rahman. The decision effectively passed into Abd al-Rahman's hands. Abd al-Rahman asked **Imam Ali** and Uthman for a promise to act justly and to obey whoever was chosen.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 18i2n4z
Abd al-Rahman b. Awf
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.5.art.actors.2.label: 1m9a3ex

scenes.6.text: Abd al-Rahman asked **Imam Ali** to pledge allegiance on the Book of God, the sunna of the Prophet and the way of the two caliphs. Bay'a is a pledge of allegiance. Imam Ali said, "The Book of God, the sunna of the Prophet and my own ijtihad." When the same condition was offered to Uthman, Uthman accepted. The pledge was made to him. **Imam Ali** did not exchange his right at Ghadir for the way of the two caliphs.

scenes.7.text: The pledge was made to Uthman. The shura is a consultative council. In the Shiqshiqiyya sermon, **Imam Ali** describes their counting him as one of those six. He also says that the arrangement of the shura affected the outcome from the very start. From Saqifa to the shura, his right was again set aside. He chose patience.

sunni.0.says: Caliph Umar is wounded; he designates Ali, Uthman, Zubayr, Talha, Sa'd and Abd al-Rahman b. Awf; Zubayr and Talha withdraw in favor of Ali and Uthman, Sa'd in favor of Abd al-Rahman; Abd al-Rahman takes a promise from both to rule with justice and obey whoever is chosen, chooses Uthman, and Ali pledges allegiance.
sunni.1.says: Caliph Abu Bakr's consultation with Abd al-Rahman b. Awf and Uthman; the objection of a group of Companions about Caliph Umar's harshness (seen secondarily in an IslamQA summary).
sunni.2.says: Caliph Abu Bakr's testament, Caliph Umar's shura, Abd al-Rahman's condition of "the Book of God, the sunna, the conduct of the two shaykhs," and Ali's answer "my own ijtihad" (it has variants).
sunni.3.says: Talha's objection to Caliph Umar's appointment (seen secondarily as an attribution on WikiShia and various sites).
sunni.4.says: Details of the shura and Uthman's pledge.
shia.0.says: Imam Ali's complaint about the handing over of the caliphate, Caliph Umar's shura and his being counted as one of them. The text could not be read in this session; the summary is from WikiShia.
shia.1.says: The claim that the sermon appears with a chain of transmission in sources before al-Radi (from a WikiShia summary; the books themselves were not opened).
shia.2.says: A Mu'tazili commentator; he says he saw the sermon in the works of authors before al-Radi such as al-Balkhi and Ibn Qutayba (WikiShia report).
shia.3.says: The Shia understanding of imamate and reports on the shura; not verified in this session.
disputes.0.title: gr3wv8
Can a caliph appoint his own successor?
disputes.0.sunni: Caliph Abu Bakr chose Caliph Umar in his place; this appointment is narrated in the sources. In the Sunni reading, this is a legitimate path through the benefit of the Ummah and the acceptance of the Companions.
disputes.0.shia: Caliph Abu Bakr chose Caliph Umar in his place; this appointment is narrated in the sources. In the Shia reading, the place of the caliphate lies with Imam Ali through the testament at Ghadir.
disputes.1.title: 50n32k
The six of the shura
disputes.1.sunni: Caliph Umar designated six people; this appears in Bukhari (Bukhari, Sahih, no. 3700). In the Sunni reading, he broadened the consultation by choosing people with whom the Prophet was pleased, and the result was completed with Medina's approval.
disputes.1.shia: The six appear in Bukhari (Bukhari, Sahih, no. 3700). In the Shia reading, Imam Ali's being treated on a par with the others and the authority remaining with Abd al-Rahman b. Awf are mentioned in the Shiqshiqiyya as an arrangement that affected the outcome from the start.
disputes.2.title: ihla63
Imam Ali's answer to the condition of conduct
disputes.2.sunni: Al-Tabari reports that Imam Ali said "my own ijtihad." In the Sunni reading, this is his preservation of his scholarly independence.
disputes.2.shia: Al-Tabari reports that Imam Ali said "my own ijtihad." In the Shia reading, he did not bind himself to the practice of the two earlier caliphs but took the Book, the sunna and his own ijtihad as the basis.
questions.0: Caliph Abu Bakr's choice of Caliph Umar stands in the sources. What does reading this appointment calmly, together with Imam Ali's place, make you think?
questions.1: Caliph Umar counted Imam Ali among the six. How do you think a heart that loves his place before the Prophet reads this shura?
questions.2: The decision gathered in the hands of Abd al-Rahman b. Awf and Uthman was chosen. What does thinking about this picture with the love felt for Imam Ali remind you of?
questions.3: Imam Ali said "my own ijtihad." How does his standing by his own knowledge alongside the Book and the sunna deepen love for him?
summary: Caliph Abu Bakr chose Caliph Umar in his place. When Caliph Umar was wounded, he left a six-man shura; Abd al-Rahman b. Awf chose Uthman. In the Shia reading, this shura, Imam Ali's saying "my own ijtihad" and the Shiqshiqiyya describe his place.
key: A caliphate by appointment, a narrowed shura
notes.0: Before dying, Caliph Abu Bakr appointed Caliph Umar as caliph.
notes.1: When Caliph Umar was wounded, he left the matter to a six-man shura.
notes.2: The members of the shura were: Imam Ali, Uthman, Zubayr, Talha, Sa'd and Abd al-Rahman b. Awf.
notes.3: Imam Ali did not accept Abd al-Rahman's condition, and Uthman was chosen.
notes.4: Imam Ali's complaint about this process appears in the Shiqshiqiyya sermon in Nahj al-Balagha.
